To accurately capture these environments with cameras, exposure compensation (also known as bracketing) is necessary to ensure all scene details remain visible. This study examines the simultaneous over- and underexposure brackets along a series of standard exposures to determine the optimal capture sequence for a set of high-exposure images. Leveraging these brackets, a new technique recovers a cleaner and more complete high-exposure image from multiple captures where certain details remain overexposed. Additionally, this work introduces a method for enhancing overexposed regions utilizing underexposed and exposed images through training on paired datasets. Collectively, these approaches enable the acquisition of detailed, well-exposed photography in complex high-light scenarios.
